expectations.name: interactive-non-atomic-on-approved-srd
expected_behavior: States the approval gate in one clause from `Status: ACCEPTED` and starts editing — never asks the user to confirm or override it, and asks no glossary question before a proposal touches a term

Names STA-4 in the proposal and makes clear that approving it means the authority has agreed, not merely that the user wants the edit — folded into the one confirmation, not asked as a second question
Front-loads a grouped issue summary, then walks entry by entry
Proposes the split with location, before/after, and a one-line rationale

Prepares the split as an add-only change — a new `GR-3c` rather than a renumber — and leaves it unapplied: the SRD contains no `GR-3c` after the run, because the authority STA-4 names has not agreed to it
Applies nothing: the SRD is byte-identical after the run and no decision log exists, because the authority never agreed

expectations.name: apply-a-review-file
expected_behavior: Parses the findings and works them blocker → major → minor
Fixes each finding through the edit loop — one change, confirm, re-validate — referring to findings by number, and says after each applied change what its re-validation found
Leaves `login.review.md` untouched: `review` owns that file
Closes by pointing at `review specs/login.md check` to tick off what landed, plus the manifest of what changed and what was left flagged

expectations.name: targeted-edit-by-description
expected_behavior: Locates the matching requirement and confirms the match before editing anything
Proposes a verifiable replacement — a measurable threshold — per REQ-5/6, with before/after; the figure comes from the user or stands as a named placeholder, never one the run made up
Re-validates that entry and its cross-references after applying, and reports whether anything new broke

expectations.name: polish-leaves-metadata-and-meaning
expected_behavior: Confirms each mechanical fix — British → US spelling, keyword caps, stray example text — and applies none silently
Rewrites no requirement meaning and restructures nothing
Fills no Owners, Initiative, or Designs field and does not touch `Status`; flags those gaps instead
Closes with the manifest of the mechanical changes made

expectations.name: terse-output
expected_behavior: Opens each proposal with the change itself — location, before/after, rule id — with no preamble, restatement of the request, or narration of what it is about to do. The front-loaded issue summary is required and is not preamble
The closing manifest lists approved edits one line each, rather than re-narrating diffs the user already saw
Points at `specs/login.decisions.md` — the SRD path with `.md` replaced, not `login.md.decisions.md` — instead of re-printing its contents

expectations.name: generate-in-scope-on-signal
expected_behavior: Before the signal, never flags SCO-2 against the marker and never fabricates scope items

On the signal, derives candidates from the requirement groups and gives none of them an `SC-n`; a positional label ("candidate 3") is fine. `SC-1…n` are assigned only as the confirmed set replaces the marker, so a dropped or merged candidate renumbers nothing
Walks the candidates point by point for the user to keep, reword, merge, split, or drop
Replaces the marker with the confirmed items and re-runs the SCO-2/3 coverage check

expectations.name: add-to-todo-on-demand
expected_behavior: Appends to the existing `## TODO` section as the next numbered item, renumbering nothing above it
Skips the propose-and-confirm loop — the instruction is the confirmation
Renumbers nothing else and reports only the single line added
At session end, flags the non-empty `## TODO` as a follow-up blocking `ACCEPTED`

expectations.name: autofix-bulk-applies-errata
expected_behavior: Acts on nothing outside the `## Errata` block: no mechanical issue absent from it is fixed, and the SRD is not re-scanned for new ones
Runs neither the glossary resolution nor the approval gate — errata touch neither ids nor terms — so no `Status` clause and no glossary question reach the user, and no `glossary_terms` call is made
Lists the three substitutions and takes one confirmation for the whole batch, not the per-change loop
Verifies each `old` at its anchor, applies the two that match exactly once, and reports the third as stale rather than guessing where it belongs
Writes no review file and invokes no `review` run; prints the exact hand-off command `review specs/login.md check #n #n`, scoped to the two applied errata, for the user to run
Closes with a manifest naming what was applied, what was skipped and why, and the findings handed to `check` — not what `check` later did with them

expectations.name: interactive-from-a-line-number
expected_behavior: Runs session start, then resolves line 210 to the entry at or nearest it instead of front-loading a whole-document summary
Begins the entry-by-entry walk there and continues in document order to the end
Still runs the closing consistency pass over the whole document, not just the walked tail

expectations.name: feedback-from-a-finding-number
expected_behavior: Enters at finding #2 rather than at the top of severity order
After each finding resolves or is skipped, defaults to the next by number
Jumps to any number the user names out of order, resumes the ascending walk from there, and after the highest number returns to the lowest one still open
Leaves the review file untouched and closes by pointing at `review specs/login.md check`

expectations.name: corpus-grounded-edit-routes-the-unconfirmable
expected_behavior: Searches the corpus before accepting the edit, and the draft gap it hands over names the queries tried
Captures the gap with `srd:report-doc-gap` as a draft silently — no interruption and no grilling mid-edit
States the retry count as a fact inside the proposal, so the user's `YN` attests it and `srd:kb` receives it — the fact is in front of the user when the key is pressed, not looked up afterwards
Asks no separate "bank this?" question
Hands the unconfirmable claim to `srd:report-doc-gap` and the attested fact to `srd:kb`, and neither interrupts the edit in progress

expectations.name: session-start-drains-prior-drafts
expected_behavior: Runs the draft check, finds the two drafts, and invokes `srd:report-doc-gap` to surface their count and topics before any edit
Offers to work them now
On a defer, proceeds into the normal interactive run — issue summary, then the walk — and leaves both drafts on the server for the next start

expectations.name: decision-log-written-per-edit
expected_behavior: Appends the applied change to `specs/login.decisions.md` before proposing the next one: the entry is in the file by the turn that puts the next proposal, so nothing is lost if the session dies mid-flow
Creates the file with `cfsync-plugin: ignore-push` front matter on the first write
Records the entry, the change in prose, and the user's reason quoted verbatim — never paraphrased, never a diff, and never a rationale neither the user nor the proposal stated
Does not log the skipped proposal
The closing manifest points at the file's newest session block as the author's summary

expectations.name: removal-on-an-approved-srd
expected_behavior: Does not delete `GR-6`: on an approved SRD a removal strikes the text through and keeps the identifier (STA-8)
Leaves the number in place and renumbers nothing after it (STA-7)
Records the removal in `<srd>.decisions.md` like any other applied edit

expectations.name: finding-outside-the-mandate
expected_behavior: Enters at `#2`, recognizes it is outside the mandate, and says so rather than opening a proposal it cannot apply
Names it as the author's to fix and advances to the next finding by number
Leaves the review file untouched
Carries it into the closing manifest as flagged and left

expectations.name: autofix-writes-the-decision-log
expected_behavior: Writes one decision-log entry per applied substitution — the batch path logs like every other applied edit
Creates `specs/login.decisions.md` with its `cfsync-plugin: ignore-push` front matter on the first write
Refuses the third erratum because its `old` occurs twice in the anchor — not uniquely located — applies the other two, and names the reason it refused
Each log entry is prose naming the entry and what changed, under a dated `##` session block — never a diff

expectations.name: open-questions-and-read-only-comments
expected_behavior: Leaves the comment block byte-for-byte unchanged — comment text is verbatim history, never edited, answered, or rewritten
Does not treat the `GR-9` reference as a broken cross-reference to repair, and does not renumber anything to make it resolve

Carries the unanswerable question in a numbered `## Open questions` list kept in the terminal reply, and the closing manifest reproduces that numbered list rather than a bare count — never written into the SRD as a section
Does not trail the proposal with it as an aside, and does not make answering it a precondition for the rest of the run — a skip on that entry is not the same as blocking

expectations.name: no-drafts-skip-the-delegates
expected_behavior: The closing manifest's start clause reports that the draft check found none and that neither `srd:report-doc-gap` nor `srd:kb` ran
Asks no approval-gate question: reads `IN PROGRESS`, says so in one clause, and proceeds

Asks no glossary question and calls no `glossary_terms`: the target names no term, and the run must not spend a call on one it never reaches. The fix's figure is not made up: with none in the SRD or from the user, the proposal carries a named placeholder
Re-validates `GR-2`'s cross-references after applying, and the closing re-check covers the whole document
Reaches the first proposal in its first or second turn, with no setup question and no narrated startup sequence

expectations.name: feedback-without-a-review-file
expected_behavior: Says the review file is absent and stops: `#n` names a finding only a review file can carry
Invents no findings and proposes no edit of its own, even though the SRD has real defects
Leaves `specs/login.md` unchanged and writes no decision log
Says it in one or two lines naming the missing file, and reports nothing about its own start — no approval-gate line, no draft-check result, no closing manifest
Offers no menu of other ways in (run `review`, paste findings, drop the argument): the user asked for a finding number, and the answer is that there are none
